testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, you should:

options.text: Take quick glances at the mirrors.
Look at the mirrors for long periods of time.
Use only the rearview mirror.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take quick glances at the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel far down the road without watching where you are going.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time.
Is encouraged on long trips.
Takes your attention away from driving.
Is required so cargo stays watched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid distracted driving, do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Anything that diverts your attention from the road is a distraction.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Push down the brake pedal.
Open the hood.
Release air from the air storage tanks.
Open the cab door.

questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. The brakes can be damaged if both springs and air pressure are applied at the same time.

questions.question: Fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns must be kept for:

options.text: One year.
Two years.
Three years.
Four years.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicle operators must register under the IFTA program. Fuel and mileage records supporting IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns must be kept for four years.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use the windshield wipers.
Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights.
Use the air conditioning.

questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Use them even during the day.

questions.question: The steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with both hands.
Held with one hand so you can eat or drink.
Held with one hand at a time, switching back and forth.
Cracked to improve your grip.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands to control your vehicle. Your hands should be on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, you should:

options.text: Use hands-free cell phone devices.
Text instead of call on your cell phone.
Not use your cell phone.
Turn up the volume on your cell phone.

questions.explanation: Heavy traffic requires your full attention. Avoid all distractions, including cell phone use.

questions.question: While operating a CMV:

options.text: You are not required to wear a safety belt.
You only need a safety belt if the vehicle has no airbags.
You only need a safety belt if carrying more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a safety belt.
questions.explanation: A safety belt is your best protection in a crash. You must always wear a safety belt when operating a CMV.

questions.question: If a pre-trip inspection finds something unsafe, you should:

options.text: Finish the trip and call a mechanic after.
Have a more experienced driver take the truck.
Get it fixed right away.
Stop using the unsafe parts but keep driving.

questions.explanation: You must repair any unsafe item found during a pre-trip inspection. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: No more than two times.
Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
Only after going up a hill.
Only after a hard stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or every three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. You are responsible for keeping cargo safely secured during the trip.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire rim is damaged?

options.text: Leave it on the vehicle.
Weld it to fix the damage.
Replace it.
Move it to the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded to repair damage are not safe to use.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may show that a driver is:

options.text: Driving while impaired.
Not dressed warmly enough.
Using the heat in the vehicle.
Enjoying fresh air.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. A driver with an open window in cold weather may be impaired.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will stick.
The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The brakes may stop working.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: Brakes get hot when used. If they get too hot from overuse, they expand and change chemically. This makes them less effective and eventually causes them to stop working. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: Why do dry bulk tanks need special care?

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.
Loads are usually stable.
They are usually overloaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and their loads often shift during travel. Be especially careful when turning or going around curves.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should you use your four-way flashers?

options.text: Turn them on before crossing railroad tracks.
Never use them.
Only use them after crossing railroad tracks.
Only use them near railroad tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off once your entire vehicle has passed the tracks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of header boards?

options.text: They should never be used.
They protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
They protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.
They provide extra storage space.

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: What should a driver do if their vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it.
Get out and walk away from the tracks.
Try to flag down another vehicle for a push.
Wait in the vehicle for a police officer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave it immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call that number or call 911.

questions.question: On the on-road driving test, which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks.
Stopping behind crosswalks.
Driving in the leftmost lane when multiple lanes are available.
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the leftmost lane when multiple lanes are available.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, and stop signs. On roads with multiple lanes, complete turns in the correct lane. Always use or stay in the rightmost lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system is not working properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes may escape from the rear of the muffler.
It may prevent proper steering.
It may cause problems if the trailer is fully loaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper area of a vehicle. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Prevent the front tires from skidding.
Prevent the front tires from overheating.
Create equal brake usage.
Remove doubt when applying the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have front brake limiting valves designed to reduce the risk of front wheel skidding. However, research shows these devices are not necessary, so they should be left in the "normal" position.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat, you may hear a loud bang. When does the truck get affected?

options.text: Right away.
After a few seconds.
Only if the flat tire is in the front.
Only if the truck is carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: There is usually a delay of a few seconds between hearing the tire fail and feeling the truck respond. Because of this delay, you might think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: What does Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) mean?

options.text: The total weight of the vehicle plus its cargo.
The total weight of just the tractor.
The total weight of just the loaded trailer.
The total weight of the tractor and trailer without cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the vehicle plus its cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of the vehicle and all its cargo combined.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid driving aggressively?

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Tailgate other vehicles.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Do not make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make hand gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan trips with extra time for traffic delays. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane. Do not make gestures at other drivers, even small ones like shaking your head.

questions.question: A 40-foot-long item on a flatbed trailer needs at least how many tie-downs?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. All cargo must have a minimum of two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: How should cargo be secured on flatbed trailers?

options.text: Tied down.
Glued down.
Left loose.
Pushed to one side.

questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to keep it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: What should you do when checking the engine?

options.text: Keep the parking brake off.
Place wheel chocks under the wheels.
Leave the engine running.
Put the gear in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place wheel chocks under the wheels.
questions.explanation: Before checking the engine, set the parking brake and/or place wheel chocks under the wheels. Check the engine before getting in the cab and starting the engine.

questions.question: How many driver's licenses can one person have?

options.text: Two—one for cars and one for trucks.
Only one.
One for each state where you plan to drive.
A car license from one state and a CDL from another state.

questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one license. States share driver information in a computer database to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, what should the driver do?

options.text: Ignore the report and find issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic right away.
Read and review the report.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and just rely on the report.

questions.explanation: Start your inspection by reading any previous inspection report. The company should have already fixed any problems listed in the report.

questions.question: Why should you do the pre-trip inspection steps in the same order every time?

options.text: You are less likely to skip a step.
You will finish faster.
The law requires it.
The inspection form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are less likely to skip a step.
questions.explanation: Following the same order every time helps you learn the steps and remember them all. A routine makes it less likely you will forget something.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which is NOT required?

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Complete the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, you must drive safely, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without accidents or traffic violations.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles need ____ to change gears.

options.text: Double clutching
Double shifting
Triple clutching
Triple shifting

questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions need double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator and push in the clutch while shifting to neutral. Release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the right speed. Then push in the clutch again, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: When you do the stop/start maneuver during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to get onto the shoulder.
Not use any turn signals.
Slam on the brakes to stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down smoothly.

questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you will pull your vehicle to the side of the road and stop. Check traffic, use your turn signal, slow down evenly with smooth braking, change gears as needed, and come to a full stop without coasting.

questions.question: If your air tanks have manual drains, how often should you drain them?

options.text: Every day
Once a week
Once a month
Once every 3,000 miles

questions.explanation: Drain your air tanks at the end of each day to prevent oil and water from building up.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Formally ask you to fix your vehicle's problems.
Call a mechanic.
Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a vehicle unsafe, they can remove it from service until it is fixed.

questions.question: If you drive in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license should you get?

options.text: Either excepted or non-excepted
Excepted
Non-excepted
Traditional

questions.explanation: If you drive in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must get a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are found:

options.text: Only at the front wheels.
Only at the rear wheels.
Only at the driver's side wheels.
At all four wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are at all four wheels. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: The air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold enough air for only one brake use.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 brake uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: You should cover cargo:

options.text: To protect it from thieves.
To protect it from weather.
To keep other drivers from seeing what you are carrying.
To keep your cargo a secret.

questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive a CMV with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.01 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.04 percent.
0.08 percent.

questions.explanation: Driving a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal. You will lose your license for at least one year for a first offense. If you drive with any alcohol in your system below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: To avoid slowing down traffic while driving a heavy vehicle, you should:

options.text: Change gears while driving uphill.
Try to pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane.
Use your brakes while driving downhill.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle's weight prevents it from keeping up with traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: What can happen if your vehicle has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It may get better fuel mileage.
It may be hard for you to see the road.
It may tip over.
The tires may not handle the weight.

questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity is very important. A high center of gravity (like cargo piled high or heavy cargo on top) makes your vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:

options.text: Not use the brake pedal.
Press the accelerator.
Move the steering wheel.
Be extra careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Which type of brakes do most heavy-duty vehicles have?

options.text: Air brakes
Solid brakes
Liquid brakes
Gravity brakes

questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems for safety.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible.
Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk to make other drivers move out of your lane.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or overweight loads need special permits. You may have driving restrictions, like only driving at certain times.

questions.question: When using road speed to know when to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work best for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and try to keep pace.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as a guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work best for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Learn which speeds work best for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: The maximum safe play on a 20-inch steering wheel is:

options.text: One-quarter of an inch.
Two inches.
10 inches.

questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be unsafe. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving:

options.text: Braking will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
You can drive normally and check the brakes later.
You should keep driving but turn on flashers to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking will only work if there is enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure light turns on, stop and park safely as soon as possible. Braking will only work as long as enough air is left in the tanks.

questions.question: States verify that a CDL or CLP driver has only one license by:

options.text: Making phone calls to surrounding states.
Using a computer system that connects all states.
Asking the driver.
Looking through the driver's wallet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using a computer system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP information in a shared computer database. When you apply for a license in one state, they check this database to make sure you don't already have one in another state.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible on the axles.
Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
Not worry about how the weight is distributed.
Only put weight on the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight should be balanced evenly. Too much or too little weight on an axle affects vehicle control and can damage the axle.

questions.question: A header board is used to:

options.text: Help a driver see behind them.
Protect the driver from moving cargo.
Provide extra storage space.
Prevent the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect drivers from cargo that shifts during a crash or emergency stop.
